ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side of the center node is connected to +6 V through a 2 kΩ resistor; above the center node there is a current source labeled 1 mA, with the arrow pointing downward, and this current source injects current into the center node; the center node is connected downward to ground through an ideal diode V1, and the current I1 is marked as downward; the right side of the center node is connected to the +3 V terminal through an ideal diode V2, and I2 is marked as to the right. Reasoning: +6 V through the 2 kΩ resistor will make the center node tend to be at a positive potential relative to ground, and at the same time the upper 1 mA current source also sends current into the center node. Therefore V1 is forward biased, and the ideal diode V1 clamps the center node at 0 V. When the center node is 0 V, the other end of V2 is +3 V, so V2 is reverse biased and does not conduct, I2 = 0. The current flowing from the left +6 V branch through the 2 kΩ resistor into the center node is (6 - 0) / 2 kΩ = 3 mA; the current source additionally injects 1 mA into the node. By KCL, these 3 mA + 1 mA must flow downward through V1, so I1 = 4 mA.

method.method_draft: Identify that the +6 V branch through 2 kΩ and the 1 mA source tend to drive the central node positive relative to ground, so V1 is forward biased and clamps the node to 0 V. The +6 V branch supplies (6−0)/2 kΩ = 3 mA into the node, and the current source supplies another 1 mA into the node. By KCL, these must leave through V1, so I1 = 3 mA + 1 mA = 4 mA.

method.method_draft: Test possible diode states. If both diodes were open, the 1 mA source would force current through the 2 kΩ resistor toward the +6 V node, giving an unconstrained node voltage of 8 V, which would forward-bias both diodes, so this is inconsistent. If V2 alone were on, the node would be clamped near +3 V, which still forward-biases V1 to ground, so V2-only is inconsistent. If both were on, ideal shorts would try to clamp the same node to both 0 V and +3 V, impossible. Therefore the only consistent state is V1 on and V2 off. Then the central node is at 0 V, the +6 V/2 kΩ branch contributes 3 mA into the node, and the current source contributes 1 mA, so KCL gives I1 = 4 mA downward.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中中央节点向左通过一个 2 kΩ 电阻接到 +6 V；中央节点上方有一个 1 mA 电流源，箭头向下，表示向中央节点注入 1 mA；中央节点向下通过理想二极管 V1 接地，标出的 I1 方向向下；中央节点向右通过理想二极管 V2 接到 +3 V，标出的 I2 方向向右。推理：按二极管状态测试。若 V1、V2 都截止，1 mA 电流源注入中央节点后只能经左侧 2 kΩ 电阻流向 +6 V，因此节点电压需为 6 V + (1 mA)(2 kΩ) = 8 V，这会使 V1 对地正向偏置，也会使 V2 对 +3 V 正向偏置，矛盾。若仅 V2 导通，则中央节点被钳位到 +3 V，此时 V1 上端为 +3 V、下端接地，V1 仍会正向导通，矛盾。若 V1、V2 都导通，理想短路会要求同一中央节点同时为 0 V 和 +3 V，不可能。因此唯一一致状态是 V1 导通、V2 截止。此时中央节点为 0 V，左侧 +6 V 经 2 kΩ 向节点提供电流 (6-0)/2 kΩ = 3 mA，电流源再向节点提供 1 mA。由 KCL，流过 V1 向下的电流 I1 = 3 mA + 1 mA = 4 mA。
